_comment: Per-machine config. config.json is gitignored. bootstrap.sh seeds config.json from this file only when config.json does not exist, and NOTHING writes config.json afterwards — only a human edits it. Pinned engine/tokenizer/GGUF/simplex-chat refs live in the committed pins.json, not here. Every machine keeps its own config.json.

navigation._comment: Navigation is two-stage at BOTH levels and the guards are the create doors (no threshold gate). Category: the softmax offers each existing category WITH its description (bare names carried no signal) plus create_category; confirm_category_fit then confirms the winner's scope (phase navigate:category_scope, P(covers) >= category_tau) and a rejected winner authors a new category. Leaf: the softmax offers only existing skills; confirm_skill_fit then compares the winner's action to the request (phase navigate:intent, P(same) >= intent_tau) and a mismatch authors a new leaf. Both taus are separate from the top-level tau so tuning reuse-vs-create does not move run assessment/fidelity. The check is deliberately permissive: with real descriptions in-scope requests score 0.9-1.0, so a borderline over-cover routes into a plausible category and the leaf guard catches it.

engine._comment: Per-machine engine settings only. The pinned engine/tokenizer/GGUF refs (semif_repo, semif_ref, gguf_url, gguf_sha256, source, revision) live in the committed pins.json — bumped on update, never per-machine config. The GGUF path is derived from pins.json's engine.gguf_url under .runtime/models/; set `gguf` here only to override it with a custom path.

llm._comment: Small OpenAI-compatible model that authors a new category/skill title + description (never the runnable body — that is `codegen` below). Deliberately its own endpoint/model, so it can be local and fast even when codegen is remote. Runs on THIS machine's local ollama; bootstrap reads base_url/model from here (a --llm-url/--llm-model flag overrides for that run only) and pulls `model` if it is missing. `model` is required (no default): set it to a model the endpoint serves. Uses the same provider machinery as codegen (real SSE stream, token budget, idle watchdog); short JSON replies. Sampler params (temperature/top_p/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty) are opt-in: an unset value is omitted from the request so the server's model default applies — set them here only when you know the right values for the model. The draft is authored asynchronously by a single-slot worker and the request re-runs when it lands; an unreachable endpoint is graceful (traced, user notified), not fatal. disable_thinking sends reasoning_effort:none so a reasoning model answers the short JSON directly instead of spending the reply budget on hidden chain-of-thought (set false only for an endpoint that rejects the parameter). provider selects the transport: "ollama" (default; a local OpenAI-compatible server, context auto-detected via /api/show) or "opencode" (the hosted OpenCode Console inference API at https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1 — set model to a Chat Completions family id such as kimi-k2.7-code or glm-5.3, and provide api_key or api_key_env; the ollama probe is skipped).

codegen._comment: OpenAI-compatible model that writes runnable skill bodies. Runs on a REMOTE ollama host (bootstrap reads base_url/model from here; a --codegen-url/--codegen-model flag overrides for that run only); the local small model is `llm` above. `model` is required (no default): set it to a code-capable model the endpoint serves. Bodies perform real actions against the user's configured services via stdlib transports, read every operational value from ctx.config, and declare their integration (INTEGRATION: service/transport/config_vars). Larger/slower than the decision or title/description model. The transport always streams so the client-side token budget (output cap / peak total fill) can abort a runaway in real time; stream only toggles console echo of tokens. timeout is total seconds; idle_warn/idle_timeout surface a silent (wedged) stream. The context window is auto-detected via ollama /api/show; context_window is the manual fallback (0 = auto/default 100000). smart_limit/warn_limit and max_fill_ratio/warn_fill_ratio bound total fill; max_output caps streamed output (>=1 absolute tokens, 0<x<1 fraction of window); chars_per_token converts chars to the token estimate. temperature/top_p/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty are opt-in: an unset value is omitted from the request so the server's model/Modelfile default applies; set them here only when you know the right values for the model. A rejected body retries with a fresh short prompt (max_attempts attempts), reusing the same sampler params. elicitation asks the product owner implementation questions before the body is written (posted to the question queue; every front end defers). After the body lands it is reviewed for real-action fidelity, then the data contract (contract.json) is derived in a separate call, then skill.test.py (hermetic mechanics test: loopback http.server for HTTP bodies, fixtures inline, no external network) in a shared-context call, and the test is auto-run as a subprocess (test_timeout seconds); on failure a 3-option SemIf decision (code/contract/test) regenerates the failing piece, bounded by test_max_attempts. contract_search.enabled auto-populates the skill config.json via SemIf against the global + category config. provider selects the transport: "ollama" (default; local OpenAI-compatible server, context auto-detected via /api/show) or "opencode" (the hosted OpenCode Console inference API at https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1 — set model to a Chat Completions family id such as kimi-k2.7-code, glm-5.3, or deepseek-v4.1-flash, and provide api_key or api_key_env; the ollama probe is skipped).

elicitation._comment: Ask the product owner implementation questions before the body is written: which service/account, how to connect, where the credential comes from, what success looks like. Every front end defers questions to the questions panel; the single-slot writer asks them one at a time and waits answer_timeout seconds for each (the clock resets on every answer submit, so the user only ever sees the next question after answering the current one; a timeout stops the sequence). wait_timeout is the separate, longer wait for the optional creation-approval gate. Questions never ask for operational data values (collected at first fire) or config-vs-input cadence (the config step owns that).

fidelity._comment: After the body lands, an authoring:fidelity SemIf decision (accept/reconsider, P(reconsider) >= tau or any static finding) checks whether it really performs the action vs simulates it (canned result, fabricated data, draft-by-default). Static INTEGRATION checks (declaration vs code) run alongside. The gate never diagnoses: a rejected body is regenerated with the raw evidence bundle, bounded by max_attempts; a still-fake body is accepted but traced/badged, never a hard authoring failure.

repair._comment: A failed real run triggers a logged SemIf repair choice (retry / repair_skill / ask_user / no_repair) surfaced in the REPL and dashboard. Executing a repair is user-confirmed (a codegen write is slow); body repairs are bounded by max_attempts per skill and carry the observed failure into the regeneration.

contract_search._comment: After the data contract lands, run a SemIf choice per variable to auto-populate the skill config.json from the global config and the category config (data/skills/<category>/config.json). Logged as phase config:search.

degeneration._comment: SemIf degeneration watchdog: while the body streams, a 2-option SemIf decision (continue/stop) is made every `interval` chars against the last `window` chars of content+reasoning (once `min_chars` have accumulated); P(stop) >= threshold aborts the write with a graceful stub. Recorded trace-only (kind `codegen`), never in the decision log. Disabled when no engine is available.

simplex_chat._comment: Per-machine simplex-chat daemon settings. The pinned binary (version/bin_url/sha256) lives in the committed pins.json, not here. The command gateway talks to the daemon on `port` (profile .runtime/simplex/, unit semif-simplex.service). The SimpleX forwarding bridge owns its OWN daemon/profile on `forward_port` (profile .runtime/simplex-forward/, unit semif-simplex-forward.service) so messaging UX never shares the command bot's identity. bootstrap.sh renders both units from these values. gateway.simplex.ws_url must match `port`; bridges.simplex.ws_url must match `forward_port`.

bridges._comment: Standalone third-party API bridges: a simple, secure local HTTP layer between codegen-authored skill bodies and real system services. Each bridge runs as its own process (`python -m semif_agent.cli bridge [--name NAME]`), one process per service daemon, and never runs inside the command gateway — gateway isolation is non-negotiable (see AGENTS.md). The bridge catalog (names, endpoints, config vars) is injected into the code-generation prompts via `semif_agent.bridges.describe_bridges()`.

simplex._comment: SimpleX forwarding bridge: buffers every inbound DM (no allowlist — the point is to see who reached the bot through its invite link), and serves invite-link / read / send over HTTP. It owns its own simplex-chat daemon/profile (`ws_url`, `forward_port` above), separate from the command gateway's. Skills use the top-level `simplex_bridge_url`; keep it in sync with host/port. Binds localhost only; an optional `token` is required in the X-Semif-Token header when set.

gateway._comment: Messenger COMMAND intake — and nothing else. `python -m semif_agent.cli gateway` connects to the command simplex-chat daemon (`simplex_chat.port`) over its JSON WebSocket API and feeds authorized DM text through the normal gate/score/queue/dispatch pipeline; results, authoring questions, and repair offers are sent back to the originating chat. It must never read a contact's history, show/create invite links, or compose on the user's behalf — that is the independent bridge services' job (`bridges`). Requires the optional `websockets` package (lazy-imported; the gateway refuses to start without it). allowed_users entries match either a numeric contactId or a display name; default is deny-all unless allow_all_users is set. home_channel receives messages whose origin chat is unknown (e.g. a background repair offer). text_batch_delay concatenates rapid-fire messages from one contact. Groups/attachments are not supported in this first cut.
